To extract information out of the body-of-contract (BOC): * There is an overarching clause numbering that identifies what the clause is and where it is to in the whole body of contract. * KeyWords: Keywords used across all contracts of that type, across industries. * Topics(Tags): Themed-topics for all that data(keywords) The extract data points is used to train a NLP(natural-language processing) model that will then process un-annotated clauses to extract facts from such text and insert into a database(relational, key-value type). ## Contract Anonymizer ### Contract Anonymizers #### 1. _Contract Information_ The contract information (clause numbering and topic themed-tags) and a small set of initial Keywords used for searching in the database of annotations for related/similar annotated information and the text of the clause/subject. ![alt text](/img/WAGTAIL_contract_information.jpg) #### 2. Clause-keywords database To make sure there is enough of examples for training data. A clause in WAGTAIL has an entry in an annotation database of key-value fields and also there is the text the clause, it self. For example: The sample of database annotation in relation to keyword "Warranty": ![alt text](/img/Anonymization_Keywords_01.png) To ensure to training has as complete and varied as data as possible for it to train an algorithm, in this way all key-value data with same keywords can be put together in one table: ![alt text](/img/Anonymization_Database.png) #### 3. Keyword Extract-Annotate(Extract Clauses) NLP model will search all contract(keyword) database for keyword and produce the result of clauses(text) with matched keyword as an answer(output). ![alt text](/img/WAGTAIL_Anonymization_Search_Cloasess-2.png) #### 4. Sentiment Analysis Sentiment is analysis is used to determine how a customer and user(party) in general, perceives and feelings of such service provisioned with the company. Such data points can be gathered at each milestone of agreement/partnership such the service provision, to gain better understanding where each service delivery and productivity and customer satisfaction(NPS) scores, where to apply resources needed for any continuous improvement of services offered to the client. This process helps to determine where more service quality improvements need to be made, in order to ensure client satisfaction is met: ![alt text](/img/sentiment_analogy.jpg) #### 5. Agreement Term Extraction Term is extracted from the body of contract by NLP and saved into database to be used further for any other automated processes, it self. ### Workflow

Answer: It is a common question here:  https://stackoverflow.com/questions/18571318/how-to-generate-output-from-a-regex-match-in-python
But the answers usually come back that they don't really answer the question for the general case.
But: they give a glimpse to the solution.

There are several strategies, but the best in practice would be first to match `\w+\((\w+)\)/(\w+)/` and the extract the `group()` results `print(m2.groups())`; but that takes much longer.

Here's my proposed regular-expression solution, because it is so simple:  First remove all leading whitespace except for newlines with a `$` (all whitespace except for linefeed chars). Then split the first word after the first `=` (the contract name) on whitespace. This will produce two words on success (`0`-length is acceptable); then extract the first word (from `\[[\w]+(\])?/(\w+)`, which is what will follow an equals sign in a contract, with optional brackets) and the last word (from `[[\w]+(/?|\n?)/[\s]*\]]`) because one or both will probably be longer than 7 characters, to get the 30+ unique groups which have lengths of less than seven characters. Then just take the first index (`indx=str.split()[1].index(r"`) of each 35+ length `regex` string in the set of those to remove the groups with non-yes answers, then test with `.isdigit()` to see if a group has a digit, then finally make a 0 (so all groups are 0 digits), then append a \strong{Yes/N} indicator, with \strong{Y} for Yes and \strong{N} for No; then append this to your main result set, that for the lines with Yes/No answers.

The regular expression is,

# Features:
- Support both multi-level and one-level nested questions
- NLP approach to question selection
- Handling multiple solutions
- Handling complex multiple-choice questions with several options
- Handling different units and abbreviations for question options
- Handling both time interval and time interval questions (ex. When a customer will arrive?)

# Motivation:
[This work describes the first effort toward an automated legal code generation from large data (e.g. contract clauses). The proposed algorithm can be helpful to both legal experts and novices, and the results can guide a future effort on automated extraction.] 
Prior to [this work](https://www.tumblr.com/d/d5325a47-fdbe-4305-bdf3-3f533bbc676a/p8n1yq2y4g9uxt0x33e2b3b72s26u0m6i-i5q26qn2j8s7wbv), extraction and classification  is mainly hand-crafted. In addition, many approaches fail to produce clean, high-quality text due to noisy data or require expert knowledge in extraction.

# Data:
The project collects a new [contract dataset](http://lcag.hci.seu.edu.cn/download) of Chinese legal documents containing 2,925 unique questions from 318 real contracts, which is publicly available. The dataset contains Chinese version of the contracts with annotation of the natural-language questions with no missing data and [the gold answer](http://lcag.hci.seu.edu.cn/download) (the answers are from human readers in this dataset, who manually selected what they believed was the best option for the question). For the project we only use the Chinese version because English dataset [NLP2020](https://competitions.codalab.org/competitions/12513) contains annotations for the gold text, answers and question.

# Preparing the questions: 
Since [NLP2020](https://competitions.codalab.org/competitions/12513) annotations contain only one line of information per example which makes it difficult for humans to verify the correctness of the annotation, our project takes some measures: [first](http://lcag.hci.seu.edu.cn/data_processing/en_preprocess.txt) we remove punctuations, spaces and stop words, and then run the text through [Word Aligned Language Model Embeddings](http://lcag.hci.seu.edu.cn/document/Word aligned language model embedding.pdf). Finally the words are passed through a bi-linear perceptron of logistic regression and are given 2 as the correct answer, other answers get 0 as incorrect. 

# Preparing the gold answer: In the preparing of the dataset we remove some questions that we feel are not relevant for our final project. We do this by the following steps ([in brief]: We delete all question and answers that match each other, remove all duplicates questions (where one word of question and all words of answer are the same). Also, we delete all questions that only contain numbers without any words).
After this stage we apply the method of [Sakai and Doshi (2020)](http://lcag.hci.seu.edu.cn/document/Sakai and Doshi (2020).pdf) to add the gold answer (the answers provided by humans on the [NLP2020](https://competitions.codalab.org/competitions/12513) dataset) to the dataset.

"A warranty is a guarantee that meets three specific criteria: 
    • It is a promise from one party about the characteristics of a product or other object.
    • The promise is in writing and includes some standard form language, such as “Low price is guaranteed for one year.”
    • The recipient has some right to claim a breach and, therefore, some redress.
In all three respects, warranties of products and services differ markedly from warranties under the common law—that is, from promises about behavioral obligations between individuals.
(1) A warranty of a product's specific properties is limited to those which, ordinarily, do not arise from an ordinary buyer-seller transaction. 
  
  
(2) Any guarantee about a product's characteristics must be in writing to have force and effect. 
  
  
(3) The standard-form nature (the use of an "all goods or services are ‘guaranteed’ to conform with the standard warranty that . . . ”; a promise written on the order form, invoice, package, tag, or the like; the inclusion of a standard-language promise in the standard form written warranty) distinguishes warranties from "other assurances". 
  
  
Such special assurances include representations or promises made by individuals and entities which were meant to have their ordinary force and effect and promises made in writing that lack the formal features required for a warranty.
Mere assurances are not treated as warranties under the general principles and rules discussed above."

2.  If a word has a vowel at least 2x times, then word is a correct match according to vowel pattern. The number of a vowel times has some patterns (like `2`) and we can use regular expressions `Pattern` on this type of problem and return a value of `String` with a match in `"(^ | \\S).$"`

def nf(n : Int):
  vw : Iterator[String] = "abcdefghjklmnprst".chars.toSeq.iterator
  acc : Iterator[Boolean] = vw.zip(Seq.fill[Boolean](n+1)(True):_*)
  while acc.nonEmpty:
    val (word, f) = acc.next
    if f then "".filter(!w => 'a' <= w && w <= 'z').count(p => false) <= f:
      acc.replace(w.char, f) = w:
  acc

def pattern:
  "^\\s*(^ | \\S)".r.pattern.map({_.group}).to(Set)

def read:
  val qs : Queue[String] = Queue.single("""\d{2,}-"","""")
  qs.dequeue
    case a
